common_uses: Atopic dermatitis; asthma; chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps and other labeled type-2 inflammatory conditions
potential_benefits: Reduces type-2 inflammation in approved conditions
important_risks_or_adverse_effects: Injection-site reactions; conjunctivitis/eye inflammation; eosinophilia; hypersensitivity
dosage: Dose varies by age and indication; subcutaneous dosing is used
half_life_or_body_presence: About 17–20 days terminal half-life
who_can_use: Patients who meet the approved indication and age criteria
important_precautions: Prescription medicine; use according to the prescribing information

common_uses: Crohn's disease; ulcerative colitis; rheumatoid arthritis; ankylosing spondylitis; psoriatic arthritis; plaque psoriasis
potential_benefits: TNF-alpha blocker that reduces inflammatory activity
important_risks_or_adverse_effects: Serious infections; infusion reactions; malignancy warnings; liver injury
dosage: IV infusion; dose and interval vary by indication
half_life_or_body_presence: About 8–10 days terminal half-life
who_can_use: Patients with an approved indication under specialist supervision
important_precautions: Screening and monitoring for infections such as TB are important

common_uses: Many corticosteroid-responsive inflammatory and allergic conditions
potential_benefits: Powerful anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effect
important_risks_or_adverse_effects: Infection risk; increased blood glucose; fluid retention; osteoporosis; adrenal suppression
dosage: Dose is highly indication-dependent; tapering may be required after prolonged treatment
half_life_or_body_presence: Prednisone is converted to prednisolone; prednisolone plasma half-life is roughly 2–4 hours
who_can_use: Patients with clinician-diagnosed corticosteroid-responsive conditions
important_precautions: Do not stop prolonged treatment suddenly without medical advice

common_uses: Type 2 diabetes in adults as an adjunct to diet and exercise
potential_benefits: Improves blood-glucose control through GIP and GLP-1 receptor activity
important_risks_or_adverse_effects: Nausea; diarrhea; vomiting; decreased appetite; pancreatitis and gallbladder warnings
dosage: Usually starts at 2.5 mg once weekly and is increased gradually; maximum labeled dose 15 mg weekly
half_life_or_body_presence: About 5 days half-life
who_can_use: Adults with the labeled type 2 diabetes indication
important_precautions: Prescription medicine; follow contraindications and monitoring requirements

common_uses: Certain cancers; rheumatoid arthritis; severe psoriasis and other labeled conditions
potential_benefits: Antimetabolite and immunomodulatory treatment
important_risks_or_adverse_effects: Serious bone-marrow, liver, lung, kidney and gastrointestinal toxicity; embryo-fetal toxicity
dosage: Dose and frequency vary greatly by indication; some non-cancer uses are once weekly
half_life_or_body_presence: Plasma half-life is roughly 3–10 hours; intracellular metabolites may persist longer
who_can_use: Patients with a specific labeled indication under close medical supervision
important_precautions: Medication-frequency errors can be dangerous; follow the exact prescription

common_uses: Chronic weight management in eligible adults; obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity under current labeling
potential_benefits: Supports weight reduction and metabolic improvement in approved indications
important_risks_or_adverse_effects: Nausea; diarrhea; vomiting; gastrointestinal effects; pancreatitis and gallbladder warnings
dosage: Usually starts at 2.5 mg once weekly with gradual increases; maximum labeled dose 15 mg weekly
half_life_or_body_presence: About 5 days half-life
who_can_use: Adults who meet the approved indication and clinical criteria
important_precautions: Prescription medicine; use only as directed

common_uses: Certain B-cell cancers; rheumatoid arthritis; granulomatosis with polyangiitis; microscopic polyangiitis; pemphigus vulgaris
potential_benefits: Depletes CD20-positive B cells
important_risks_or_adverse_effects: Infusion reactions; serious infections; hepatitis B reactivation; rare PML
dosage: IV dosing varies substantially by indication
half_life_or_body_presence: Half-life varies by regimen and indication and can range from days to weeks
who_can_use: Patients with approved indications under specialist care
important_precautions: Infection screening and monitoring are important

common_uses: Moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease
potential_benefits: Gut-selective anti-integrin therapy that reduces intestinal inflammation
important_risks_or_adverse_effects: Infections; headache; nausea; arthralgia; infusion reactions
dosage: IV infusion commonly at weeks 0, 2 and 6, then every 8 weeks for many adults
half_life_or_body_presence: About 25 days terminal half-life
who_can_use: Patients with labeled inflammatory bowel disease indications
important_precautions: Monitor for infection and hypersensitivity

common_uses: Rheumatoid arthritis; giant cell arteritis; systemic sclerosis-associated ILD; selected juvenile arthritis; CRS and other labeled uses
potential_benefits: IL-6 receptor blocker that reduces inflammatory activity
important_risks_or_adverse_effects: Serious infections; liver abnormalities; low blood counts; lipid changes; gastrointestinal perforation risk
dosage: Dose varies by indication, body weight and route
half_life_or_body_presence: Half-life is concentration-, route- and indication-dependent; several days to weeks
who_can_use: Patients meeting the approved indication and age criteria
important_precautions: TB/infection screening and laboratory monitoring are important

common_uses: Temporary relief of minor aches and pains and reduction of fever
potential_benefits: Pain-relieving and fever-reducing effect
important_risks_or_adverse_effects: Liver injury with overdose or excessive total daily intake; severe skin reactions are rare
dosage: Dose depends on product, age and weight; follow the product maximum
half_life_or_body_presence: About 2–3 hours in healthy adults
who_can_use: Adults and children when the specific product label permits
important_precautions: Avoid duplicate acetaminophen-containing medicines and excess dosing

common_uses: Ulcerative colitis and rheumatoid arthritis; selected juvenile arthritis uses
potential_benefits: Reduces inflammation and disease activity
important_risks_or_adverse_effects: Nausea; headache; rash; blood-count abnormalities; liver injury; hypersensitivity
dosage: Oral dose is indication-specific and commonly increased gradually
half_life_or_body_presence: Parent drug and metabolites have different elimination times
who_can_use: Patients with labeled inflammatory conditions
important_precautions: Blood counts and liver monitoring may be required

common_uses: Treatment or prevention of folate deficiency and certain megaloblastic anemias
potential_benefits: Restores folate needed for normal cell production
important_risks_or_adverse_effects: Usually well tolerated; rare hypersensitivity
dosage: Dose depends on the reason for treatment and formulation
half_life_or_body_presence: Plasma elimination is relatively short, while body folate stores turn over more slowly
who_can_use: People with an appropriate indication for folate supplementation
important_precautions: Cause of deficiency should be assessed because folate can mask some B12 deficiency

common_uses: Pain and fever relief; some prescription regimens use it for antiplatelet treatment
potential_benefits: Analgesic, antipyretic, anti-inflammatory and antiplatelet effects
important_risks_or_adverse_effects: Stomach bleeding; ulcers; allergic reactions; increased bleeding risk
dosage: Dose depends strongly on indication and formulation
half_life_or_body_presence: Aspirin has a short plasma half-life, but platelet inhibition lasts for the life of affected platelets
who_can_use: Use depends on age, indication and clinician/product labeling
important_precautions: Children and teenagers with viral illness should not use aspirin unless specifically directed

common_uses: Palliative treatment of advanced prostate cancer
potential_benefits: Suppresses testosterone production in androgen-dependent prostate cancer
important_risks_or_adverse_effects: Hot flashes; injection-site reactions; metabolic/cardiovascular effects; initial tumor-flare effects
dosage: Depot subcutaneous formulations are given at intervals such as 1, 3, 4 or 6 months depending on strength
half_life_or_body_presence: Depot exposure lasts weeks to months; simple plasma half-life does not describe the depot effect
who_can_use: Adults with advanced prostate cancer for the labeled indication
important_precautions: Tumor flare and metabolic/cardiovascular effects require clinical monitoring

common_uses: Rheumatoid arthritis; psoriatic arthritis; polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis and selected prophylaxis uses
potential_benefits: Modulates T-cell co-stimulation to reduce immune-mediated inflammation
important_risks_or_adverse_effects: Infections; headache; nausea; infusion/injection reactions; hypersensitivity
dosage: IV weight-based or subcutaneous dosing varies by indication and age
half_life_or_body_presence: About 13 days terminal half-life
who_can_use: Patients meeting the approved indication and age criteria
important_precautions: Monitor for infection; combination with other biologic immune therapies may increase risk

common_uses: Rheumatoid arthritis; psoriasis; inflammatory bowel disease and multiple other inflammatory diseases
potential_benefits: TNF-alpha blocker that reduces inflammation
important_risks_or_adverse_effects: Serious infections; TB; hepatitis B reactivation; injection-site reactions; malignancy warnings
dosage: Subcutaneous dosing varies by indication; many adult regimens use 40 mg every other week
half_life_or_body_presence: About 2 weeks terminal half-life
who_can_use: Patients meeting an approved indication and eligibility criteria
important_precautions: Screen for infection/TB and follow indication-specific dosing

common_uses: Relief or prevention of bronchospasm in asthma and reversible obstructive airway disease
potential_benefits: Relaxes airway smooth muscle and improves airflow
important_risks_or_adverse_effects: Tremor; nervousness; headache; fast heartbeat; low potassium
dosage: Dose depends on inhaler/nebulizer formulation and patient age
half_life_or_body_presence: Systemic plasma half-life is roughly 3.8 hours for albuterol
who_can_use: Patients with an appropriate labeled airway indication
important_precautions: Use prescribed inhaler technique and frequency; frequent rescue use needs clinical review

common_uses: Allergic asthma; chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps; chronic spontaneous urticaria; food allergy in labeled patients
potential_benefits: Binds IgE and reduces IgE-mediated allergic inflammation
important_risks_or_adverse_effects: Anaphylaxis; injection-site reactions; headache and hypersensitivity
dosage: Subcutaneous dose depends on indication, body weight and other factors
half_life_or_body_presence: About 26 days half-life
who_can_use: Patients meeting the specific approved indication and dosing criteria
important_precautions: Administration and observation must follow prescribing guidance because of anaphylaxis risk

common_uses: Allergic rhinitis symptoms and chronic urticaria
potential_benefits: Antihistamine that reduces sneezing, itching, runny nose and hives
important_risks_or_adverse_effects: Drowsiness or fatigue; dry mouth and other effects can occur
dosage: Typical adult OTC dose is 10 mg once daily; age and kidney function can change dosing
half_life_or_body_presence: About 8–9 hours in adults; longer with kidney impairment
who_can_use: Adults and children when the specific product label permits
important_precautions: Kidney impairment may require dose adjustment; drowsiness can affect alertness

common_uses: Many corticosteroid-responsive inflammatory, allergic and other conditions
potential_benefits: Potent anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive corticosteroid
important_risks_or_adverse_effects: Infection risk; increased blood glucose; mood changes; osteoporosis; adrenal suppression
dosage: Dose varies greatly by disease and route
half_life_or_body_presence: Biological half-life is about 36–54 hours
who_can_use: Patients with a clinician-diagnosed condition for which corticosteroid therapy is appropriate
important_precautions: Longer courses require monitoring and should not be stopped abruptly without medical advice

common_uses: Vitamin D supplementation and prevention or treatment of vitamin D deficiency, depending on the product and clinical need
potential_benefits: Supports calcium absorption, bone mineralization and normal muscle and immune function
important_risks_or_adverse_effects: Excessive intake can cause vitamin D toxicity and high blood calcium, which may lead to nausea, weakness, thirst, frequent urination and kidney problems
dosage: Dose depends on age, vitamin D status, indication and product strength; follow the specific product label or clinician's advice
half_life_or_body_presence: 25-hydroxyvitamin D, the main blood marker of vitamin D status, has a circulating half-life of about 15 days
who_can_use: People who need vitamin D according to age, nutritional status or medical advice; the appropriate dose depends on the individual and product
important_precautions: Do not exceed the recommended amount; people with certain medical conditions or taking interacting medicines may need medical supervision
source: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements; DailyMed

common_uses: Treatment of hypertension; reduction in the risk of myocardial infarction, stroke, or cardiovascular death in certain high-risk patients; and treatment of stable heart failure after myocardial infarction
potential_benefits: Lowers blood pressure and, in appropriate labeled patients, can reduce certain cardiovascular risks and heart-failure-related outcomes
important_risks_or_adverse_effects: Cough, dizziness, low blood pressure, increased potassium, changes in kidney function, and angioedema can occur; fetal toxicity is an important warning
dosage: For hypertension, the labeled initial dose is 2.5 mg to 20 mg once daily, adjusted according to blood-pressure response. Other indications use different dosing schedules.
half_life_or_body_presence: Ramipril is converted to the active metabolite ramiprilat. Ramiprilat has an apparent elimination half-life of about 9 to 18 hours, with a prolonged terminal phase of more than 50 hours
who_can_use: Patients with an approved indication who are evaluated and treated under appropriate medical supervision
important_precautions: Ramipril can cause fetal injury during pregnancy. Blood pressure, kidney function, and potassium may require monitoring; dose adjustments may be needed in some patients

common_uses: Treatment of erosive esophagitis associated with GERD, maintenance of healing of erosive esophagitis, and pathological hypersecretory conditions including Zollinger-Ellison syndrome
potential_benefits: Reduces stomach acid production and helps heal or control acid-related conditions covered by the approved labeling
important_risks_or_adverse_effects: Headache, diarrhea, nausea and abdominal discomfort can occur; longer-term PPI therapy has additional risks described in the prescribing information
dosage: For adults with erosive esophagitis associated with GERD, a current delayed-release tablet label recommends 40 mg once daily for up to 8 weeks; other conditions use different regimens
half_life_or_body_presence: The terminal elimination half-life of pantoprazole is approximately 1 hour
who_can_use: Adults and, for certain labeled uses, pediatric patients 5 years and older who meet the approved indication and dosing criteria
important_precautions: Use according to the specific prescription and formulation; check contraindications and important drug interactions in the prescribing information

common_uses: Treatment of active rheumatoid arthritis in adults
potential_benefits: Helps reduce the signs and symptoms of rheumatoid arthritis and can improve physical function
important_risks_or_adverse_effects: Liver injury, diarrhea, nausea, rash, hair loss, high blood pressure, low blood-cell counts, infections and other serious adverse effects can occur
dosage: Recommended maintenance dose is 20 mg once daily. In selected patients at low risk for hepatotoxicity and myelosuppression, treatment may include 100 mg once daily for 3 days as a loading dose before 20 mg once daily
half_life_or_body_presence: Leflunomide is converted to the active metabolite teriflunomide, which has a median half-life of about 18–19 days. Without an accelerated elimination procedure, it may take up to 2 years for levels to fall below a specified threshold
who_can_use: Adults with active rheumatoid arthritis who meet the approved indication and are treated under medical supervision
important_precautions: Contraindicated in pregnancy and severe hepatic impairment. Liver function, blood pressure and blood counts should be monitored. An accelerated drug-elimination procedure may be required in certain situations

common_uses: Rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, plaque psoriasis, and certain pediatric inflammatory conditions covered by the approved labeling
potential_benefits: Blocks tumor necrosis factor (TNF) and reduces signs and symptoms of approved inflammatory diseases
important_risks_or_adverse_effects: Serious infections, injection-site reactions, tuberculosis, hepatitis B reactivation, allergic reactions and other serious risks described in the prescribing information
dosage: For adults with rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, or ankylosing spondylitis, 50 mg once weekly is a labeled regimen. Adult plaque psoriasis uses 50 mg twice weekly for 3 months, then 50 mg once weekly. Pediatric dosing depends on weight and indication
half_life_or_body_presence: The mean serum elimination half-life is approximately 102 hours (about 4.25 days) after a 25 mg subcutaneous dose
who_can_use: Patients who meet an approved indication and applicable age criteria under medical supervision
important_precautions: Screening for tuberculosis and monitoring for infections are important. Live vaccines should generally be avoided during treatment, and certain combinations with other immune therapies may increase risk

common_uses: Relief of pain and inflammation in appropriate conditions, depending on the formulation
potential_benefits: Helps reduce pain and inflammation
important_risks_or_adverse_effects: Stomach irritation, ulcers, gastrointestinal bleeding, cardiovascular risks, kidney problems and allergic reactions can occur
dosage: Dose depends on the formulation, condition and patient; follow the specific product or prescription instructions
half_life_or_body_presence: Elimination time depends on the formulation and route of administration
who_can_use: Patients with an appropriate indication and formulation under medical guidance
important_precautions: Use according to the specific product directions and medical advice; NSAID warnings and contraindications apply

common_uses: Moderate to severe plaque psoriasis, active psoriatic arthritis, active ankylosing spondylitis, active non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis, enthesitis-related arthritis, and moderate to severe hidradenitis suppurativa in patients who meet the approved criteria
potential_benefits: Reduces inflammation by blocking interleukin-17A and can improve symptoms and disease activity in approved inflammatory conditions
important_risks_or_adverse_effects: Nasopharyngitis, diarrhea, upper respiratory tract infections, injection-site reactions, hypersensitivity reactions, and increased risk of infections can occur
dosage: Dose depends on the indication, age, body weight, and route. For adult plaque psoriasis, a labeled regimen is 300 mg by subcutaneous injection at Weeks 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4, then every 4 weeks
half_life_or_body_presence: Secukinumab has a mean elimination half-life of approximately 22 to 31 days
who_can_use: Patients who meet an approved indication and applicable age and clinical criteria under healthcare-provider supervision
important_precautions: Evaluate patients for tuberculosis before starting treatment. Avoid live vaccines during treatment. Use caution in patients with inflammatory bowel disease and monitor for serious infections and hypersensitivity reactions

common_uses: Crohn's disease, rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis, plaque psoriasis, and polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis in patients who meet the approved criteria
potential_benefits: Reduces inflammatory activity by blocking tumor necrosis factor (TNF)
important_risks_or_adverse_effects: Serious infections including tuberculosis, injection-site reactions, hypersensitivity reactions, and other serious risks described in the prescribing information
dosage: Administered by subcutaneous injection. Dose depends on the condition; for adults with rheumatoid arthritis, the labeled regimen is 400 mg initially at Weeks 0, 2 and 4, followed by 200 mg every other week, with 400 mg every 4 weeks as a possible maintenance regimen
half_life_or_body_presence: Terminal elimination half-life is approximately 14 days
who_can_use: Patients who meet an approved indication and applicable age and clinical criteria under healthcare-provider supervision
important_precautions: Patients should be evaluated for tuberculosis and monitored for infections. CIMZIA should not be started during an active serious infection. Hypersensitivity and heart-failure warnings also apply

common_uses: Rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, plaque psoriasis, hidradenitis suppurativa, and certain uveitis and juvenile idiopathic arthritis indications covered by the approved labeling
potential_benefits: Blocks tumor necrosis factor (TNF) and reduces inflammatory activity in approved conditions
important_risks_or_adverse_effects: Serious infections including tuberculosis, injection-site reactions, allergic reactions, hepatitis B reactivation, and other serious risks described in the prescribing information
dosage: Subcutaneous injection. For adult rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, and ankylosing spondylitis, a labeled regimen is 40 mg every other week. Other conditions use different indication-specific dosing schedules
half_life_or_body_presence: Mean terminal half-life is approximately 2 weeks, with reported values ranging from about 10 to 20 days
who_can_use: Patients who meet an approved indication and applicable age and clinical criteria under healthcare-provider supervision
important_precautions: Patients should be evaluated for tuberculosis before treatment and monitored for serious infections. Follow the prescribing information for contraindications, vaccination guidance, and other warnings
